rv.q: It is both a beautifully clear production and one which, through the alternate casting, adds to the bottomless mystery of Pinter's play.
This way round, it has a raw intensity and haunting mystery which the other permutation doesn’t achieve.
One of the theatrical treats of the year would be to see Old Times twice, with each of the casting arrangements.
Rickson’s production charts all these shifting tonal alliances with exquisite good taste...

cn.t: A classy, brilliantly clear revival of Pinter's cryptic memory play, elevated by potent performances from Scott Thomas and Williams alternating roles. The production illuminates the text's mysteries while showcasing its interpretive richness.
